source: NCERT Class VI, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 9.

sections.heading: 1. Why Separate Substances
points: We separate the components of a mixture to **remove harmful/useless parts**, **obtain useful components**, or **remove impurities**.
A **mixture** contains two or more substances not chemically combined.
The method chosen depends on the **properties** of the components (size, weight, magnetism, solubility).

sections.heading: 2. Separating Solids from Solids
points: **Handpicking** — remove small quantities of larger impurities by hand (e.g. stones from rice).
**Threshing** — separate grain from stalks by beating.
**Winnowing** — separate heavier grain from lighter husk using **wind/air**.
**Sieving** — separate components of **different sizes** using a sieve (e.g. flour from bran).
**Magnetic separation** — remove **iron** particles using a magnet.

sections.heading: 3. Separating Solids from Liquids
points: **Sedimentation** — heavier insoluble solid settles at the bottom (the settled solid = **sediment**).
**Decantation** — carefully pour off the clear liquid above the sediment.
**Filtration** — pass through a filter to separate **insoluble** solids (e.g. tea leaves; sand from water).
**Evaporation** — remove a **soluble** solid by evaporating the liquid (e.g. **salt from seawater**).

sections.heading: 4. Solutions and Saturation
points: A **solution** = a soluble solid dissolved evenly in a liquid (the **solvent**).
A **saturated solution** = one in which **no more** solute can dissolve at that temperature.
**Heating** usually lets **more** solute dissolve; **condensation** can recover the evaporated liquid (distillation idea).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Winnowing uses wind to separate lighter husk from heavier grain.
Sieving separates by particle size; magnetic separation removes iron.
Sedimentation → solid settles; decantation → pour off clear liquid; filtration → removes insoluble solids.
Evaporation recovers a soluble solid (salt from seawater).
Saturated solution = no more solute dissolves at that temperature; heating dissolves more.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Filtration** removes **insoluble** solids; a **dissolved (soluble)** solid passes through the filter — use **evaporation** for that.
**Winnowing** uses **air/wind**; **sieving** uses **size** difference.
**Sedimentation** = settling; **decantation** = pouring off — two steps often used together.
Salt is obtained from seawater by **evaporation**, not filtration.
